exposure: 0.05% chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG) irrigation during cesarean delivery
cohort: Patients undergoing cesarean delivery at a community hospital, divided into a treatment group receiving CHG irrigation and a control group not receiving it, totaling 351 and 432 deliveries respectively.
finding: The study found no significant difference in overall post-cesarean surgical site infection (SSI) rates with CHG irrigation, but a significant increase in endometritis was observed in the CHG irrigation group.
mod_finding: The study found no significant difference in overall post-cesarean SSI rates when performing intra-abdominal and subcutaneous irrigation with CHG solution during cesarean delivery, but a significant increase in endometritis was observed with the use of CHG irrigation.
